subject: sociology
title: Education & Class: Internal School Factors
welcome_lead: Inside the school — labels, sets and pupil identities shape outcomes.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology education class internal labelling streaming subculture Willis.
final_note: School can reproduce inequality even when families don't.

concepts.def: Teachers attaching meanings to pupils based on impressions.
Label becomes reality through behaviour change.

walkthroughs.body_html: Becker (1971): teachers judged middle-class pupils as 'ideal'. Rist (1970) US kindergarten study: teachers seated pupils by background after 8 days, shaping outcomes. Rosenthal & Jacobson (1968) 'Pygmalion': random 'gifted' label produced 12 IQ point gain in juniors. SFP at work.

Lacey (1970) Hightown Grammar: differentiation (sorting by ability) leads to polarisation (anti vs pro-school subcultures). Ball (1981) Beachside Comprehensive: replacement of streaming with mixed-ability reduced anti-school subcultures but middle-class kids still advantaged.

Willis (1977) ethnography of 12 Hammertown 'lads': rejected school via mucking about, found masculine pride in unskilled jobs. They 'partly penetrated' capitalism but reproduced their own position. Bowles & Gintis (1976) correspondence theory: hidden curriculum mirrors workplace.

mcqs.q: Rosenthal & Jacobson's 1968 study showed teacher expectations produced effects in which type of pupils?
Willis studied how many 'lads' in his 1977 ethnography?

numericals.q: In what year did Willis publish 'Learning to Labour'?
